--- title: "Multiple Regression" subtitle: "PSYC 6019-A01 / PSYC 6022-A01
2026-11-20 | Lab 13" author: "Jess Helmer" footer: "[jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026](https://jhelmer3.github.io/PSYC6019-2026/)" format: revealjs: code-link: true slide-number: true code-line-numbers: false theme: ../../gt-theme.scss width: 1200 execute: echo: true dpi: 600 freeze: auto knitr: opts_chunk: dev: svg --- ## Outline - Visualizing regression predictions - Assumption checking - Regression diagnostics - Confounders ::: {.cell} ::: # Multiple Regression ## Multiple Regression So far, we've only examined the relationship between a continuous outcome and continuous predictor one at a time with *simple regression*. With *multiple regression*, we can examine these relationships **jointly**: looking at one relationship while adjusting for the relationships of other variables. $$y_i = \beta_0 \, + \, \beta_1 x_{1i} \, + \, \beta_2 x_{2i} \, + \, ... \, + \, \beta_p x_{2i} \, + \, \epsilon$$ ::: subpoint ○ $\beta_0$: value of $y$ when *all predictors* $x = 0$ ::: ::: subpoint ○ $\beta_1$: slope of $x_{1i}$ adjusted for the effect of $x_{2i}, \, ..., \,x_{pi}$ ::: ## Simple Regression :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(palmerpenguins) m1 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(m1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -1762.08 -446.98 32.59 462.31 1636.86 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 362.307 283.345 1.279 0.202 bill_length_mm 87.415 6.402 13.654 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 645.4 on 340 degrees of freedom (2 observations deleted due to missingness) Multiple R-squared: 0.3542, Adjusted R-squared: 0.3523 F-statistic: 186.4 on 1 and 340 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Coefficient interpretations ::: :::: ## Standardizing ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins_cleaned <- penguins |> mutate(across(ends_with("_mm"), scale)) penguins_cleaned ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 344 × 8 species island bill_length_mm[,1] bill_depth_mm[,1] flipper_length_mm[,1] 1 Adelie Torgersen -0.883 0.784 -1.42 2 Adelie Torgersen -0.810 0.126 -1.06 3 Adelie Torgersen -0.663 0.430 -0.421 4 Adelie Torgersen NA NA NA 5 Adelie Torgersen -1.32 1.09 -0.563 6 Adelie Torgersen -0.847 1.75 -0.776 7 Adelie Torgersen -0.920 0.329 -1.42 8 Adelie Torgersen -0.865 1.24 -0.421 9 Adelie Torgersen -1.80 0.480 -0.563 10 Adelie Torgersen -0.352 1.54 -0.776 # ℹ 334 more rows # ℹ 3 more variables: body_mass_g , sex , year ``` ::: ::: ## Simple Regression :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m1 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins_cleaned) summary(m1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm, data = penguins_cleaned) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -1762.08 -446.98 32.59 462.31 1636.86 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 4201.75 34.90 120.39 <2e-16 *** bill_length_mm 477.25 34.95 13.65 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 645.4 on 340 degrees of freedom (2 observations deleted due to missingness) Multiple R-squared: 0.3542, Adjusted R-squared: 0.3523 F-statistic: 186.4 on 1 and 340 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Coefficient interpretations ::: :::: ## Multiple Regression :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m2 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm + bill_depth_mm, data = penguins_cleaned) summary(m2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm + bill_depth_mm, data = penguins_cleaned) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -1804.61 -454.83 8.15 463.53 1544.82 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 4201.75 31.64 132.809 <2e-16 *** bill_length_mm 411.00 32.60 12.608 <2e-16 *** bill_depth_mm -281.85 32.60 -8.646 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 585.1 on 339 degrees of freedom (2 observations deleted due to missingness) Multiple R-squared: 0.4708, Adjusted R-squared: 0.4677 F-statistic: 150.8 on 2 and 339 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} After adjusting for bill depth, an increase in 1 SD in bill length is associated with an 411 g increase in body mass. ::: :::: ## Multiple Regression :::: {.columns} ::: {.column width="50%"} ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m3 <- lm(body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm + bill_depth_mm + flipper_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(m3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Call: lm(formula = body_mass_g ~ bill_length_mm + bill_depth_mm + flipper_length_mm, data = penguins) Residuals: Min 1Q Median 3Q Max -1054.94 -290.33 -21.91 239.04 1276.64 Coefficients: Estimate Std. Error t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) -6424.765 561.469 -11.443 <2e-16 *** bill_length_mm 4.162 5.329 0.781 0.435 bill_depth_mm 20.050 13.694 1.464 0.144 flipper_length_mm 50.269 2.477 20.293 <2e-16 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 Residual standard error: 393.4 on 338 degrees of freedom (2 observations deleted due to missingness) Multiple R-squared: 0.7615, Adjusted R-squared: 0.7594 F-statistic: 359.7 on 3 and 338 DF, p-value: < 2.2e-16 ``` ::: ::: ::: ::: {.column width="50%"} Coefficient interpretations ::: :::: ## Regression Diagnostics With multiple regression, we want to check on... - Normality of residuals + Relationships with other variables - Multicollinearity among predictors - Outliers ## Normality of Residuals # Multicollinearity ## Multicollinearity Multicollinearity refers to the ability of *predictors* to be associated with *each other*. High multicollinearity: when the predictors in the model can explain a high amount of variance in another predictor. ![](../media/lab_13/multicollinearity_gossip.png) ::: footer Image made with GPT-6 on 2026-11-12 (may or may not try to make my own to replace). ::: ## Multicollinearity Bad Sim demoing misinterpretations, variance inflation bc multicollinearity ## Superficial Check ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} penguins |> select(bill_length_mm, bill_depth_mm, flipper_length_mm) |> cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm bill_length_mm 1.0000000 -0.2350529 0.6561813 bill_depth_mm -0.2350529 1.0000000 -0.5838512 flipper_length_mm 0.6561813 -0.5838512 1.0000000 ``` ::: ::: ## Why Superficial? Sim showing that variables can have small bivariate cors but in total explain a lot of the variance in y ::: {.cell} ::: ## Squared Multiple Correlations For each predictor, we need to examine the *total amount of variance* that the remaining predictors can explain of it. $$\text{body mass} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill length} + \beta_2\text{bill depth} + \beta_3\text{flipper length} + \epsilon$$ In the models ::: subpoint $\text{bill length} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill depth} + \beta_2\text{flipper length} + \epsilon$ ::: ::: subpoint $\text{bill depth} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill length} + \beta_2\text{flipper length} + \epsilon$ ::: ::: subpoint $\text{flipper length} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill depth} + \beta_2\text{bill length} + \epsilon$ ::: what is the amount of variance the predictors (i.e., the *other predictors* in the model of interest)? We can assess the amount of variance predictors can account for in an outcome with $R^2$. ## Squared Multiple Correlations The $R^2$ of these models (again, predictors in the model of interest trying to predict each other) is called *squared multiple correlations*, $SMC$s. ::: subpoint $\text{bill length} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill depth} + \beta_2\text{flipper length} + \epsilon$ ::: ::: subpoint $\text{bill depth} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill length} + \beta_2\text{flipper length} + \epsilon$ ::: ::: subpoint $\text{flipper length} = \beta_0 + \beta_1\text{bill depth} + \beta_2\text{bill length} + \epsilon$ ::: ## Squared Multiple Correlations ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} multicoll_m1 <- lm(bill_length_mm ~ bill_depth_mm + flipper_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(multicoll_m1)$r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.4638329 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} multicoll_m2 <- lm(bill_depth_mm ~ bill_length_mm + flipper_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(multicoll_m2)$r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.3793799 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} multicoll_m3 <- lm(flipper_length_mm ~ bill_depth_mm + bill_length_mm, data = penguins) summary(multicoll_m3)$r.squared ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 0.6259358 ``` ::: ::: ## Variance Inflation Factor The presence of multicollinearity among predictors in the model increases the variance of the model estimates. We can examine this effect with Variance Inflation Factors ($VIF$s). $$VIF_p = \frac{1}{1 - SMC_p}$$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} car::vif(m3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm 1.865090 1.611292 2.673338 ``` ::: ::: VIF suggested cutoffs ## Tolerance An alternative way of looking at this is with *tolerance*, which is just the inverse of $VIF$. $$tolerance = \frac{1}{VIF}$$ ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 1 / car::vif(m3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm flipper_length_mm 0.5361671 0.6206201 0.3740642 ``` ::: ::: ## All At Once ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} olsrr::ols_coll_diag(m3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Tolerance and Variance Inflation Factor --------------------------------------- Variables Tolerance VIF 1 bill_length_mm 0.5361671 1.865090 2 bill_depth_mm 0.6206201 1.611292 3 flipper_length_mm 0.3740642 2.673338 Eigenvalue and Condition Index ------------------------------ Eigenvalue Condition Index intercept bill_length_mm bill_depth_mm 1 3.9740092816 1.00000 9.073338e-05 0.0005108682 0.0005063802 2 0.0197406728 14.18840 6.615112e-04 0.1216676763 0.2432806652 3 0.0054556972 26.98916 5.751741e-02 0.6447644340 0.1461153623 4 0.0007943484 70.73086 9.417303e-01 0.2330570215 0.6100975923 flipper_length_mm 1 0.0001146937 2 0.0094403326 3 0.0834853268 4 0.9069596469 ``` ::: ::: ## Variance Inflation Factor # Outliers ## Outlier Detection ## Outlier vs Leverage

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
